# Project Context: Content Hub V2 (Local-First Skill Engine)

## What V2 Is

A **local-first content production engine** that lives at `C:\Users\madhu\Claude cowork\Content Hub V2\`. Modeled on Chase AI's 10M-views workflow. Stops at the script — no automated rendering. Produces **9 deliverables per long-form** via 7 Claude Code slash-commands.

V2 is a **fork** of V1 (the SaaS-stack project at `C:\Users\madhu\Claude cowork\Content Hub\`). V1 is parked. V2 is where all active work happens. Decision logged in [[2026-04-28_V2_Pivot_Local_First_Engine]] (V1 vault).

## Current State — 2026-04-28

**Phase 0 (Cleanup) — not yet started.** V2 currently contains a full clone of V1 and needs SaaS layers stripped before build can begin.

See [[Current_Sprint]] for the live task list.

## Architecture (V2)

Two-layer skill pattern, repeated 7 times:

```
.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md   ← Claude Code entry point (/<name> trigger)
skills/<name>.py                 ← Python helper, calls model(s), writes to vault
prompts/<name>.md                ← Single source of truth for prompt text
```

**Cost-aware model routing:**
- **Ollama (local, free)** — first-draft outlines, structural work
- **Claude (paid)** — hooks, titles, voice cleanup, final-30-second polish
- **Gemini** — kept available for any tool that already wires it (research_service.py)

**Knowledge layer:**
- `notebooklm-py` (already cloned in V2) — programmatic NotebookLM access for one-shot Callaway masterclass extraction + ad-hoc deep research
- `Content-Hub-Vault/` (this vault) — human-facing workspace and skill output target
- pgvector RAG (`backend/research/rag.py`) kept available, deprioritized in v1

attachment.content:
- discovery-to-mvp-coach: Guide a user from a vague problem observation to an executable 21-day Manual MVP plan through structured scientific discovery: observation, causal modeling, falsifiable hypothesis, assumption testing, Mom Test interview practice, and synthetic persona stress-testing. Use this whenever someone wants to investigate or validate a problem before building, pressure-test a problem statement or idea, design a low-cost manual experiment to test a thesis, or move from observation to hypothesis to testable MVP, even if they do not name a framework. Also use when a user arrives with a completed OPT masterplan and wants to validate the problem behind that automation use case. Do NOT use when the user already has a written PRD and only needs it validated; use prd-validation-coach instead.
- notebooklm: Complete API for Google NotebookLM - full programmatic access including features not in the web UI. Create notebooks, add sources, generate all artifact types, download in multiple formats. Activates on explicit /notebooklm or intent like "create a podcast about X"
- cascade: Generate a full distribution package (blog post, Twitter/X thread, LinkedIn post) from a completed video outline+research or a YouTube URL. Use this skill whenever the user types /cascade, says "generate distribution content", "create social posts from my outline", "write a blog post from my research", "turn this into a Twitter thread and LinkedIn", "cascade this", or asks to repurpose a YouTube video into written content for multiple platforms. Also trigger when the user has just approved an outline and asks "what's next?" — cascade is the natural next step after /outline.
- context-audit: Audit your Claude Code setup for token waste and context bloat. Use when the user says "audit my context", "check my settings", "why is Claude so slow", "token optimization", "context audit", or runs /context-audit. Starts by running /context to see real overhead, then audits MCP servers, CLAUDE.md rules, skills, settings, and file permissions. Returns a health score with specific fixes.
- graphify: Turn any folder of files into a navigable knowledge graph. Use this skill whenever the user types /graphify, or says "build a knowledge graph", "graphify this", "map this codebase". Supports full pipeline, incremental --update, --query, --path, --explain, --add <url>, --wiki, --obsidian, --neo4j, --watch, --svg, --graphml flags.
- hook: Step 3 of 8 in the content pipeline (/researcher → /ideation → /hook → /outline → /title → /cascade → /short-form → /voice-cleanup). Generate 5 Kallaway-trained YouTube hook variations for a video topic — the critical first 30 seconds that stop the scroll and open a curiosity loop. Use this skill whenever the user types /hook, asks to "write hooks", "generate hooks", "create my opening", "write my intro", "give me hooks for", or mentions wanting attention-grabbing YouTube video openings. Trigger automatically when /ideation has just completed and the user has picked an idea. After generating 5 hooks, show all 5 Spoken Lines and ask the user to pick one before suggesting /outline — hook choice determines the structure of the entire video outline.
- ideation: Step 2 of 8 in the content production pipeline (/researcher → /ideation → /hook → /outline → /title → /cascade → /short-form → /voice-cleanup). Reads vault research briefs and generates 9 ranked video ideas with gap analysis, competitive reasoning, and audience desire mapping. Use this skill whenever the user types /ideation, says "generate ideas", "what video should I make", "give me video ideas", or asks what to do after research. Always trigger after /researcher completes. After showing the 9 ideas, ask the user to pick one before suggesting /hook — this choice determines the entire downstream pipeline.
- marketing-brain: /marketing-brain
- orchestrate: Multi-agent orchestration for complex tasks that span multiple domains, files, or specialists. Use this skill whenever the user types /orchestrate or /delegate, or says "orchestrate this", "dispatch agents", "delegate this", "use multi-agent", or "use the orchestrator". Also trigger automatically when the task spans 3+ subtasks, touches 2+ specialist domains (e.g. schema + backend + frontend, or any combination of roles from AGENTS.md), or involves 10+ files across subsystems. If a task touches the database AND the API AND the UI in a single request — this skill should fire. Do NOT trigger for single-domain work, one-file bug fixes, simple config changes, or exploratory investigation where the problem isn't yet defined.
- outline: Step 4 of 8 in the content production pipeline (/researcher → /ideation → /hook → /outline → /title → /cascade → /short-form → /voice-cleanup). Generates the Dopamine Ladder video script outline from an approved hook + research brief, then writes it to Content-Hub-Vault-V2/06-Outlines/. Use this skill whenever the user types /outline, says "write the outline", "build the outline", "structure the video", "create the video structure", "outline this video", "now outline it", or asks what to do after hook selection. Also trigger when the user has just picked a hook from /hook and says "what's next?", "continue the pipeline", "move forward", or "let's go" — /outline is always the next step after hook selection. Always suggest /cascade as the next step after the outline is reviewed.
- researcher: Step 1 of 8 in the content production pipeline (/researcher → /ideation → /hook → /outline → /title → /cascade → /short-form → /voice-cleanup). Runs deep content-gap research on GitHub trending repos via NotebookLM and outputs a dated research brief to Content-Hub-Vault-V2/10-Research/. Use this skill whenever the user types /researcher, says "research a topic", "find content gaps", "what should I make a video about", "check trending repos", "run research on [topic]", "I want to start a new video", or asks what to research next. Also trigger when the user wants to kick off the production pipeline from scratch — /researcher is always the entry point. Always suggest /ideation as the next step after the brief is reviewed.
- resume-orchestration: Resume an in-flight orchestration produced by the /orchestrate skill after context compaction or a killed session. Use this whenever the user types /resume-orchestration or /resume, or says "resume the orchestration", "pick up the orchestration", "continue the last orchestration". Only triggers when an active state file exists in Content-Hub-Vault/00-Management/Orchestrations/. Do NOT use to start a new orchestration — that is /orchestrate.
- run-pipeline: /run-pipeline
- short-form: Generate 3 vertical video scripts (30s, 60s, 90s) from your research + outline or a YouTube URL — step 6 of 7 in the content pipeline (/cascade → /short-form → /voice-cleanup). Use this skill whenever the user types /short-form, says "write shorts", "generate short-form scripts", "make vertical videos", "create Reels scripts", "create TikTok scripts", "repurpose this for shorts", "make short clips from this", or asks to adapt long-form content into short vertical format. Also trigger automatically after /cascade completes and the user says "what's next?", "continue", "move forward", or "next step" — /short-form is always the step after /cascade.
- title: ---
- voice-cleanup: Strip AI-isms, corporate language, and robotic phrasing from any skill output — rewrites content in the creator's authentic human voice using a detailed voice profile and banned-phrase list. Use this whenever the user types /voice-cleanup, says "de-AI this", "humanize this", "make this sound like me", "strip the AI language", "clean up the robot speak", or "voice cleanup". Also trigger automatically when the user just finished /short-form or /cascade and mentions the output sounds too formal, stiff, polished, corporate, or AI-generated — voice-cleanup is the mandatory final step before publishing anything. Supports single files, pasted text, and batch cleanup of an entire folder.
- yt-pipeline: /yt-pipeline
- om-capture-1on1: Capture 1:1 Meeting
- om-dump: Freeform capture mode. Dump anything — conversations, decisions, incidents, wins, thoughts — and I'll route it all to the right notes with proper templates, frontmatter, and wikilinks.
- om-humanize: Voice-calibrated editing — makes Claude-drafted text sound like you wrote it, not like AI wrote it.
- om-incident-capture: Incident Capture
- om-intake: Process all unread meeting notes in work/meetings/ — reads each file, classifies content, routes to the right vault notes, then clears the inbox.
- om-meeting: Prep for any meeting by topic — subject-forward briefing with open tasks, blockers, and brainstormed considerations the user may not have thought of yet.
- om-peer-scan: Peer PR Deep Scan
- om-prep-1on1: Prep for an upcoming 1:1 — load person context, surface open items, suggest agenda based on vault state.
- om-project-archive: Project Archive
- om-review-brief: Generate Review Brief
- om-review-peer: Peer Review Writer
- om-self-review: Self-Review Writer
- om-slack-scan: Slack Deep Scan
- om-standup: Morning kickoff. Load today's context, review yesterday, surface open tasks, and identify priorities.
- om-vault-audit: Vault Audit
- om-vault-upgrade: Vault Upgrade
- om-weekly: Weekly synthesis — cross-session review of vault activity, North Star alignment, patterns, uncaptured wins, and forward priorities.
- om-wrap-up: Wrap Up
- codex:rescue: Delegate investigation, an explicit fix request, or follow-up rescue work to the Codex rescue subagent
- codex:setup: Check whether the local Codex CLI is ready and optionally toggle the stop-time review gate
- skill-creator:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, update or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- frontend-design:frontend-design: Create distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces with high design quality. Use this skill when the user asks to build web components, pages, or applications. Generates creative, polished code that avoids generic AI aesthetics.
- codex:gpt-5-4-prompting: Internal guidance for composing Codex and GPT-5.4 prompts for coding, review, diagnosis, and research tasks inside the Codex Claude Code plugin
- codex:codex-result-handling: Internal guidance for presenting Codex helper output back to the user
- codex:codex-cli-runtime: Internal helper contract for calling the codex-companion runtime from Claude Code
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).

SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). """
Standalone pipeline runner — orchestrates the 9-step content production workflow.

New order (v2.1):
1. Research (yt_pipeline.py) → 10-Research/{slug}/
2. Studio reports → 11-Reports/{slug}/ (+ voice-cleanup)
3. Ideation → 02-Ideas/{slug}/ (+ voice-cleanup)
4. Hook → 05-Hooks/{slug}/ (+ voice-cleanup)
5. Outline → 06-Outlines/{slug}/ (+ voice-cleanup)
6. Title → 07-Titles/{slug}/ (+ voice-cleanup)
7. Short-form → 09-Shorts/{slug}/ (+ voice-cleanup per script)
8. Cascade → 08-Distribution/{slug}/ (+ voice-cleanup per channel)
9. Studio slides + video (from cascade) → 12-Slides/{slug}/ + 13-Video/{slug}/

Usage:
    python skills/pipeline.py "<topic>" "<url1,url2,...>"
"""

import asyncio
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path

PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).parent.parent
VAULT = PROJECT_ROOT / "Content-Hub-Vault-V2"
SKILLS = PROJECT_ROOT / "skills"

from skills import studio

# Ensure all subprocess skill scripts can import from project root
_existing = os.environ.get("PYTHONPATH", "")
_SUBPROCESS_ENV = {
    **os.environ,
    "PYTHONPATH": f"{PROJECT_ROOT}{os.pathsep}{_existing}" if _existing else str(PROJECT_ROOT),
    "PYTHONIOENCODING": "utf-8",
}


def _slug(topic: str) -> str:
    import re
    slug = re.sub(r"[^\w\s-]", "", topic.lower())
    return re.sub(r"[\s_-]+", "-", slug).strip("-")[:40]


def step(label: str, cmd: list[str]) -> int:
    print(f"\n{'='*60}", flush=True)
    print(f"[pipeline] {label}", flush=True)
    print(f"{'='*60}", flush=True)
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=PROJECT_ROOT, env=_SUBPROCESS_ENV)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        print(f"[pipeline] FAILED: {label} (exit {result.returncode})", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
    return result.returncode


def run_voice_cleanup(md_file_path: str) -> int:
    """Run voice-cleanup --inplace on a markdown file. Returns 0 on success."""
    cmd = [sys.executable, str(SKILLS / "voice_cleanup.py"), md_file_path, "--inplace"]
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=PROJECT_ROOT, env=_SUBPROCESS_ENV, capture_output=True)

VAULT_VIDEO = PROJECT_ROOT / "Content-Hub-Vault-V2" / "13-Video"

Required structure:
1. **What it is** — one paragraph, no jargon. Anchor with a one-line analogy to something the reader already knows.
2. **Why it matters** — concrete real-world impact. Name the problem it removes and what was painful before.

4. **Who should care** — 3 specific reader profiles, one paragraph each, naming the problem each profile solves with this.

Style rules: short paragraphs, no bullet-dumps, no marketing-speak ("revolutionize", "unleash", "empower"), no hedging ("might", "could potentially"). Every section opens with a clear topic sentence. Inline cite the sources. Target length: 1200–1800 words."""

TECHNICAL_PROMPT = """Write a deep-dive technical and architecture report for a senior engineer evaluating whether to adopt this in production. Goal: the reader can make a build-vs-buy decision and write an ADR after reading.

Required structure:
1. **Architecture overview** — components, responsibilities, control flow. Use a text-based diagram (ASCII or mermaid-style) showing how requests/data move.
2. **Data flow** — what moves between components, where state lives, sync vs async boundaries, ownership of mutation.

"""Subprocess executor with live stdout streaming via queue.Queue."""

import queue
import subprocess
import threading
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).parent.parent


def run_skill(cmd: list[str], log_q: queue.Queue) -> int:
    proc = subprocess.Popen(
        cmd, cwd=REPO, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
        text=True, bufsize=1, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace",
    )
    for line in proc.stdout:
        log_q.put(line.rstrip())
    proc.wait()
    log_q.put(f"__EXIT__ {proc.returncode}")
    return proc.returncode


def run_in_thread(cmd: list[str], log_q: queue.Queue) -> threading.Thread:
    t = threading.Thread(target=run_skill, args=(cmd, log_q), daemon=True)
    t.start()
    return t

"""GitHub documentation crawler — discover primary docs for a repo.

Exports:
  - DocCandidate: dataclass for discovered doc file
  - discover_primary_docs(owner_repo, token=None) -> list[DocCandidate]
"""

import os
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Optional

import httpx


@dataclass
class DocCandidate:
    """A discovered doc file candidate for inclusion as a primary source."""
    path: str  # e.g. "docs/getting-started.md"
    raw_url: str  # e.g. "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/owner/repo/main/docs/..."
    rank: int  # lower = higher priority


def _gh_headers() -> dict:
    """Build GitHub API headers, with auth if token available."""
    h = {
        "Accept": "application/vnd.github+json",
        "X-GitHub-Api-Version": "2022-11-28",
        "User-Agent": "researcher-crawler/1.0",
    }
    token = os.environ.get("GITHUB_TOKEN")
    if token:

## Deterministic systems in Content Hub V2

The codebase is split between **deterministic orchestration/IO** and **probabilistic LLM calls**. The deterministic pieces:

### 1. Pipeline orchestration (control flow)
- [skills/pipeline.py](skills/pipeline.py) — 9-step sequencer that shells out to each skill in fixed order, exit-code gated. No model decides what runs next.
- [skills/yt_pipeline.py](skills/yt_pipeline.py) — research pipeline driver.
- [app/runner.py](app/runner.py) — subprocess executor with live stdout streaming.
- [app/control_room.py](app/control_room.py) — the Control Room UI shell.

### 2. Slug + path conventions
- `_slug()` in [skills/pipeline.py:41-44](skills/pipeline.py#L41-L44) — regex-based topic→slug.
- [app/vault_index.py](app/vault_index.py) — mtime-sorted vault listings for dropdowns.

### 3. Source discovery / scraping (regex + HTTP, no LLM)
- [skills/research_sources.py](skills/research_sources.py) — arxiv/GitHub/PDF/official-docs regex extractors + reject-list for Reddit/Twitter/Medium.
- [skills/researcher_crawler.py](skills/researcher_crawler.py) — GitHub API doc-file discovery via httpx.
- [scripts/github_trending.py](scripts/github_trending.py) — daily GitHub Search API pull, 3 topic queries, writes `04-Trends/github_trending.md`.
- [skills/utils/transcript.py](skills/utils/transcript.py) — `yt_dlp` VTT subtitle extraction.

### 4. Vault I/O
- All `Content-Hub-Vault-V2/NN-*/{slug}/` directory writes — fixed folder schema (02-Ideas, 05-Hooks, 06-Outlines, 10-Research, 11-Reports, 12-Slides, 13-Video, etc.).

### 5. NotebookLM client (deterministic API wrapper)
- [notebooklm-py/](notebooklm-py/) — the SDK itself is deterministic; the *generation* it triggers (reports, slides, video, podcasts) is not.
- [skills/helpers/nlm_seed.py](skills/helpers/nlm_seed.py) — pulls suggested topics from a notebook description.

### 6. Static data + config
- [skills/data/competitor_titles.json](skills/data/competitor_titles.json), [skills/data/twitter_config.json](skills/data/twitter_config.json).
- [bin/run_control_room.bat](bin/run_control_room.bat), [bin/run_github_trending.bat](bin/run_github_trending.bat) — Task Scheduler entry points.

### Probabilistic boundaries (for contrast)
- `skills/helpers/nim_picker.py` — `pick_best_report` is an LLM call.
- `skills/utils/ai.py`, and the per-skill scripts (`hook.py`, `ideation.py`, `outline.py`, `title.py`, `short_form.py`, `cascade.py`, `voice_cleanup.py`, `researcher.py`, `studio.py`) all call models.

**The pattern:** deterministic shell wraps every LLM call. The pipeline order, slugs, paths, source extraction, and vault layout are all fixed code; only the *content generation* steps are model-driven.

content.text:
Think of the project as a **content factory**. It takes a topic and produces a full YouTube video package — research, hooks, outline, title, short clips, blog post, social posts.

The factory has two kinds of workers:

---

**The AI workers** (unpredictable, creative)
These are the LLM calls. You ask them to "write 5 hooks for this topic" and they produce something different each time. You can't predict exactly what they'll output.

---

**The deterministic systems** (the factory floor — predictable, mechanical)

These are everything else. Think of them as the factory's conveyor belts, filing clerks, and delivery trucks. They don't create anything — they just *move things around reliably*.

Here's each one in plain terms:

---

### 1. The Foreman — `pipeline.py`
Stands at the start of the factory and barks orders in sequence: "First do research, then ideation, then hooks..." If any step fails, it stops and reports the problem. It has no creativity — it just runs the same 9 steps in the same order every time.

### 2. The Assembly Line Driver — `runner.py`
When the foreman tells a worker to do something, this is the guy who literally starts them up, watches them work, and reads out their progress in real time. Pure logistics.

### 3. The Filing Clerk — `vault_index.py`
Knows exactly where everything is stored. "Show me all the research briefs, sorted by newest first." It just reads file timestamps and returns lists. No thinking involved.

### 4. The Name Tag Maker — `_slug()`
Takes any topic like "AI Agents in 2025!" and turns it into a clean folder name like `ai-agents-in-2025`. Always the same result for the same input. Pure text cleanup.

### 5. The Internet Librarian — `research_sources.py`
Reads a YouTube video description and automatically picks out the trustworthy links — arxiv papers, GitHub repos, official docs, PDFs. It also has a blacklist: Reddit, Twitter, Medium get rejected automatically. No LLM — just pattern matching (like a very precise ctrl+F).

### 6. The GitHub Scout — `researcher_crawler.py`
Given a GitHub repo, it crawls the repo structure to find the real documentation files (README, docs folder, etc.) and ranks them by importance. Mechanical — it follows fixed rules about what counts as a "primary doc."

### 7. The Daily Newspaper — `github_trending.py`
Runs every day (via Windows Task Scheduler). Asks the GitHub API "what AI repos are trending this week?" and saves the results to the vault as a markdown file. Same 3 searches, same output format, every single day.

### 8. The Subtitle Ripper — `transcript.py`
Given a YouTube URL, downloads the auto-generated captions and returns them as plain text. It doesn't understand what they say — just extracts them.

### 9. The Post Office — Vault folder structure
Every file this factory produces goes into a predictable address: `10-Research/`, `05-Hooks/`, `06-Outlines/`, etc. The addresses never change. If the AI writes a hook, the foreman puts it at `05-Hooks/{topic-slug}/`. Always.

### 10. The NotebookLM Postman — `nlm_seed.py`
Calls NotebookLM's API to fetch the suggested questions for a notebook. It's just reading back what NLM already prepared — no generation, just retrieval.

---

**The one-line summary:**

> The AI workers do the creative writing. The deterministic systems make sure every output lands in the right folder, in the right format, in the right order — reliably, every time, without fail.

"""Ideation — V2 Ranked Video Idea Generator from vault research notes."""

import asyncio, argparse, logging, sys, re
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path

PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(PROJECT_ROOT))

if hasattr(sys.stdout, "reconfigure"):
    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")

from skills.utils.ai import polish

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

RESEARCH_DIR = PROJECT_ROOT / "Content-Hub-Vault-V2" / "10-Research"
TRENDS_DIR = PROJECT_ROOT / "Content-Hub-Vault-V2" / "04-Trends"
VAULT_DIR = PROJECT_ROOT / "Content-Hub-Vault-V2" / "02-Ideas"
PROMPT_FILE = PROJECT_ROOT / "prompts" / "ideation.md"


def find_research_file(topic: str) -> Path | None:
    """Find the most recent research file matching the topic. Falls back to most recent overall."""
    if not RESEARCH_DIR.exists():
        return None

    candidates = sorted(
        [f for f in RESEARCH_DIR.glob("**/*.md") if f.name != ".gitkeep"],
        key=lambda f: f.stat().st_mtime,
        reverse=True,
    )

    if not candidates:
        return None

    # Try topic match first (case-insensitive substring)
    slug = topic.lower().replace(" ", "_")
    for f in candidates:
        if slug in f.stem.lower() or topic.lower() in f.stem.lower().replace("_", " "):
            return f

    # Fallback: most recent file
    return candidates[0]


def load_trends() -> str:
    """Load today's or most recent trending note from the vault."""
    if not TRENDS_DIR.exists():
        return ""
    md_files = sorted(
        [f for f in TRENDS_DIR.glob("*.md") if f.name != ".gitkeep"],
        key=lambda f: f.stat().st_mtime,
        reverse=True,
    )
    if not md_files:
        return ""
    content = md_files[0].read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore")
    # Truncate to keep token usage manageable
    return content[:3000]

202	}

205	# Gemini dropped 2026-05-19 — hitting 503 UNAVAILABLE consistently. Claude takes its slot.

211	    *,
212	    provider: str | None = None,
213	    model: str | None = None,

215	) -> dict:
216	    """Generate text using the AI cascade.
217	    
218	    Args:
219	        prompt: The text prompt to send
220	        provider: Force a specific provider ("gemini", "ollama", "claude")
221	        model: Force a specific model (overrides provider default)
222	        cascade: Custom cascade order (default: gemini → ollama → claude)

230	        if not func:
231	            return {"text": "", "success": False, "provider": provider, "error": f"Unknown provider: {provider}"}
232	        kwargs = {"prompt": prompt}

236	    
237	    # Cascade mode: try each provider in order
238	    chain = cascade or DEFAULT_CASCADE
239	    last_error = ""

241	        if prov_name == "ollama" and not await _ollama_available():

253	            return result

255	        logger.info("Provider %s failed (%s), trying next...", prov_name, last_error)
256	    
257	    return {"text": "", "success": False, "provider": "none", "error": f"All providers failed. Last: {last_error}"}

"""NIM-powered report suggestion picker."""

import logging
from notebooklm.types import ReportSuggestion
from skills.utils.ai import generate

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


async def pick_best_report(
    suggestions: list[ReportSuggestion],
    goal: str,
) -> ReportSuggestion | None:
    """Pick the best report suggestion from a list using NIM.

    Args:
        suggestions: List of ReportSuggestion objects from get_suggested_reports.
        goal: Either "explainer" or "technical" — the target report type.

    Returns:
        Best matching ReportSuggestion, or None if no good match found.
    """
    if not suggestions:
        return None

    # Build a prompt listing the suggestions
    suggestion_text = "\n".join(
        f"- {s.title}: {s.description}"
        for s in suggestions
    )

    prompt = f"""Given these report suggestions:

{suggestion_text}

Which one best matches the goal of creating a {goal} report?
Return ONLY the exact title of the best match (no explanation).
If none match well, return "NONE"."""

    result = await generate(prompt, cascade=["nim"])
    if not result.get("success"):
        logger.warning("NIM report picker failed: %s", result.get("error"))
        return None

    best_title = result.get("text", "").strip()
    if best_title == "NONE" or not best_title:
        return None

    # Find and return the matching suggestion
    for suggestion in suggestions:
        if suggestion.title.strip() == best_title:
            return suggestion

    logger.warning("NIM returned title '%s' but no exact match found", best_title)
    return None

Now I have a full picture. Here's the layman explanation.

---

## The Probabilistic Systems — Where the AI Actually Thinks

The factory has **7 creative workers**. Each one takes instructions (a "prompt") and generates something new. Same input, different output every time — that's what makes them probabilistic.

---

### The AI Engine Room — `skills/utils/ai.py`

Before explaining the workers, you need to know about the engine they all share.

Every AI call in the project goes through **one central switchboard**. It tries providers in order until one works:

```
1st try → Claude (Claude CLI)
2nd try → NIM (NVIDIA cloud, llama-70b)
3rd try → Ollama (local model on your machine)
```

If Claude fails or times out, it silently falls back to the next option. You never need to know which one answered — you just get text back. This is called the **AI cascade**.

---

### The 7 Creative Workers

**1. Researcher — `researcher.py`**
*"What content gaps exist in this GitHub repo?"*

Takes a trending GitHub repo, creates a NotebookLM notebook from it, then asks a series of deep questions (via NotebookLM's AI) like "what does no YouTube video cover yet?", "what are the pain points developers complain about?" It also uses **Claude** to verify that sources are credible before trusting them. Outputs a full research brief to the vault.

---

**2. Ideation — `ideation.py`**
*"What's the best video idea from this research?"*

Takes the research brief + trending repos and generates **9 ranked video ideas**. Each idea comes with: why the gap exists, what the competition missed, and what the audience actually wants. Pure LLM thinking — reads the research, reasons about the market, invents angles.

---

**3. Hook — `hook.py`**
*"Write 5 attention-grabbing opening lines for this video."*

Takes your chosen idea + research + your marketing brain knowledge file and generates **5 hook variations** trained on the Kallaway YouTube method (the first 30 seconds that stop the scroll). Two passes: `draft()` first, then `polish()` to refine. The hook determines the whole video's structure so this step matters enormously.

---

**4. Outline — `outline.py`**
*"Build the full video structure from the approved hook."*

Takes your chosen hook + research and builds a **Dopamine Ladder outline** — a specific structure where each section increases curiosity or reward for the viewer. Two LLM passes: rough draft first, then polished version.

---

**5. Voice Cleanup — `voice_cleanup.py`**
*"Make this sound like me, not an AI."*

Runs after every other step. Takes any AI-generated text and rewrites it using your voice profile + a banned-phrases list ("revolutionize", "unleash", "delve into", etc.). Single LLM call using `polish()` — Claude rewrites the content to strip robotic phrasing.

---

**6. NIM Picker — `helpers/nim_picker.py`**
*"Which of these NotebookLM report options is the best fit?"*

A tiny LLM judge. NotebookLM suggests several report formats; this calls NIM (Llama 70b) and asks "which one best matches an explainer goal?" or "which one best matches a technical goal?" Returns just the winner's title. Small decision, but probabilistic.

---

**7. Research Follow-ups — `research_plan.py` + `generate_followups()`**
*"What should I ask next based on that answer?"*

During the research phase, after each answer from NotebookLM, an LLM decides what follow-up questions to ask. It's adaptive — the question queue grows or shrinks based on what's already been answered. Budget-limited to 12 questions total to control cost.

---

### The Full Picture

```
GitHub Trending (deterministic: HTTP scrape)
        ↓
Researcher (LLM: NLM questions + Claude source verification)
        ↓
Ideation (LLM: 9 ranked video ideas)
        ↓
Hook (LLM: 5 hook variations, draft + polish)
        ↓
Outline (LLM: Dopamine Ladder structure, draft + polish)
        ↓
Title / Short-Form / Cascade (LLM: title options, vertical scripts, social posts)
        ↓
Voice Cleanup (LLM: humanize everything)
```

Every LLM call routes through the same cascade: **Claude → NIM → Ollama**. The deterministic systems move the files around. The probabilistic ones create the content.

"""Outline Skill — Generate a Dopamine Ladder video outline for a topic."""

import asyncio
import argparse
import logging
import re
import sys
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path

PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).parent.parent
if str(PROJECT_ROOT) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(PROJECT_ROOT))

if hasattr(sys.stdout, "reconfigure"):
    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")

from skills.utils.ai import draft, polish

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

VAULT_DIR = PROJECT_ROOT / "Content-Hub-Vault-V2" / "06-Outlines"
PROMPT_PATH = PROJECT_ROOT / "prompts" / "outline.md"
MARKETING_BRAIN_PATH = PROJECT_ROOT / "Content-Hub-Vault-V2" / "01-Knowledge" / "marketing_brain.md"


def load_prompt():
    if not PROMPT_PATH.exists():
        logger.error("prompts/outline.md not found at %s", PROMPT_PATH)
        sys.exit(1)
    return PROMPT_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8")


def load_marketing_brain():
    if not MARKETING_BRAIN_PATH.exists():
        logger.warning("marketing_brain.md not found — proceeding without supplemental context")
        return ""
    return MARKETING_BRAIN_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8")


def load_hook(hook_path):
    if not hook_path:
        return "(no hook provided — generate the outline structure without a specific hook)"
    p = Path(hook_path)
    if not p.exists():
        logger.warning("Hook file not found at %s — continuing without it", hook_path)
        return "(hook file not found — generate the outline structure without a specific hook)"
    return p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")


def make_slug(topic):
    slug = re.sub(r"[^\w\s-]", "", topic.lower())
    slug = re.sub(r"[\s_-]+", "-", slug).strip("-")
    return "-".join(slug.split("-")[:6])


def build_prompt(template, topic, hook, target_length, platform, marketing_brain):
    filled = template.format(
        topic=topic,
        hook=hook,
        target_length=target_length,
        platform=platform,
    )
    if marketing_brain:
        filled += f"\n\n---\n\n## KALLAWAY CONTEXT\n\n{marketing_brain[:3000]}"
    return filled


async def run(topic, hook, target_length, platform, no_polish):
    template = load_prompt()
    marketing_brain = load_marketing_brain()
    prompt = build_prompt(template, topic, hook, target_length, platform, marketing_brain)

    print("Drafting outline (NIM → Gemini)...")
    draft_result = await draft(prompt)
    if not draft_result["success"]:
        logger.error("Draft failed: %s", draft_result.get("error"))
        sys.exit(1)

    outline_text = draft_result["text"]

    if not no_polish:
        print("Polishing with NIM → Gemini → Ollama → Claude cascade...")
        polish_prompt = (
            prompt
            + f"\n\nDRAFT OUTLINE:\n{outline_text}\n\n"
            "Polish this outline: sharpen every talking point to be specific and non-generic, "
            "verify all 6 Dopamine Ladder stages are present and explicitly named, "
            "ensure [B-ROLL], [SHOW SCREEN], or [TEXT OVERLAY] markers appear in every section, "
            "and confirm Head Fakes appear at least twice. "
            "Keep the exact same format."
        )
        polish_result = await polish(polish_prompt)
        if polish_result["success"]:
            outline_text = polish_result["text"]
        else:
            logger.warning("Polish failed, using draft: %s", polish_result.get("error"))

    return outline_text


def save_output(topic, platform, target_length, hook_path, outline_text):
    slug = make_slug(topic)
    today = date.today().isoformat()
    output_path = VAULT_DIR / f"{today}_{slug}.md"
    VAULT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    content = (
        f"---\n"
        f"topic: {topic}\n"
        f"platform: {platform}\n"
        f"target_length: {target_length}m\n"
        f"hook_source: {hook_path or 'none'}\n"
        f"created: {today}\n"
        f"---\n"
        f"# Outline: {topic}\n\n"
        f"{outline_text}\n"
    )
    output_path.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")
    logger.info("Outline written to %s", output_path)
    return output_path


async def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Generate a Dopamine Ladder video outline")
    parser.add_argument("topic", help="Video topic or idea")
    parser.add_argument("--hook-path", default=None,
                        help="Path to a hook .md file from a /hook run (optional but recommended)")
    parser.add_argument("--length", type=int, default=8,
                        help="Target video length in minutes (default: 8)")
    parser.add_argument("--platform", default="yt-long",
                        choices=["yt-long", "yt-shorts"],
                        help="Target platform (default: yt-long)")
    parser.add_argument("--no-polish", action="store_true",
                        help="Skip Claude polish pass (faster, cheaper — uses draft only)")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    print(f"Outline writer: \"{args.topic}\" | {args.platform} | {args.length} min")

    hook = load_hook(args.hook_path)
    outline_text = await run(args.topic, hook, args.length, args.platform, args.no_polish)
    output_path = save_output(args.topic, args.platform, args.length, args.hook_path, outline_text)

    print(f"\n{'='*60}")
    print(f"Outline written to: {output_path}")
    print(f"{'='*60}\n")
    print(outline_text[:800])
    if len(outline_text) > 800:
        print(f"\n... (see full output at {output_path})")

Yes — the polished version is what lands in the vault, **unless the polish step fails**.

Here's the exact logic ([outline.py:93-98](skills/outline.py#L93-L98)):

1. Draft runs first → stored in `outline_text`
2. Polish runs on top of the draft → if it succeeds, **replaces** `outline_text`
3. If polish fails → falls back silently to the draft, logs a warning
4. Whatever is in `outline_text` at that point gets written to `06-Outlines/{date}_{slug}.md`

So in the happy path: polished version goes to vault. If polish errors out (API failure, timeout): draft version goes to vault instead, with a warning in the logs that you'd only see if you were watching the terminal.

One other thing worth knowing: there's a `--no-polish` flag ([outline.py:134-135](skills/outline.py#L134-L135)) that skips the polish pass entirely and saves the draft directly — faster and cheaper if you just want a rough structure.

---

description: Generate a full distribution package (blog post, Twitter/X thread, LinkedIn post) from a completed video outline+research or a YouTube URL. Use this skill whenever the user types /cascade, says "generate distribution content", "create social posts from my outline", "write a blog post from my research", "turn this into a Twitter thread and LinkedIn", "cascade this", or asks to repurpose a YouTube video into written content for multiple platforms. Also trigger when the user has just approved an outline and asks "what's next?" — cascade is the natural next step after /outline.
---

# /cascade

Turn approved research + outline (or a YouTube URL) into a ready-to-review distribution package: a blog post, Twitter/X thread, and LinkedIn post, all written to the Obsidian vault.

**Default: use your own research + outline.** This is the mode to use after you've completed `/outline`. The YouTube URL fallback is for one-off cases where you want to repurpose someone else's video.

## How to run it

### After `/outline` (preferred)

The user will typically just type `/cascade` with no extra arguments. Your job is to find the right files.

1. **Find the files.** Look in:
   - Research: `Content-Hub-Vault-V2/10-Research/` — find the most recent folder matching the topic, grab `research.md` inside it (or the dated `_brief.md` file at the root)
   - Outline: `Content-Hub-Vault-V2/06-Outlines/` — find the most recent `.md` file matching the topic
   
   If the topic is ambiguous or multiple files match, list them and ask which one.

2. **Confirm once, then run.**
   Say: "Running cascade on: [topic] — research from [filename], outline from [filename]. Go?"
   
   Wait for a yes. Then run:
   ```
   python -m skills.cascade --research-file "Content-Hub-Vault-V2/10-Research/..." --outline-file "Content-Hub-Vault-V2/06-Outlines/..." --title "<topic>"
   ```

3. **Report.** See "After completion" below.

### YouTube URL fallback

Use this when the user provides a YouTube URL and there's no research/outline for the topic.

1. Confirm: "Running cascade on: [URL]. This will extract the transcript and generate blog + Twitter + LinkedIn. Go?"
2. Wait for yes. Then run: `python -m skills.cascade <url>`
3. Report. See "After completion" below.

## After completion

Report:
- Full path to the output directory (`Content-Hub-Vault-V2/08-Distribution/YYYY-MM-DD_<slug>/`)
- The 4 files created: `blog_post.md`, `twitter_thread.md`, `linkedin_post.md`, `README.md`
- One-line preview of the Twitter hook (first tweet, ≤280 chars)
- Reminder: replace `[VIDEO_LINK]` placeholder in `twitter_thread.md` and `linkedin_post.md` before posting

Next step: `/short-form` to generate 3 short-form scripts from the same outline.

## Things to know

- **Content cap**: The helper uses up to 6,000 characters of combined research + outline. Long research files will be truncated — that's expected and fine.
- **Title**: The helper auto-extracts the title from the outline's `topic:` frontmatter field. Use `--title` to override if it picks the wrong thing.
- **If it fails**: Check that `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set in `.env` and that the research/outline paths are correct. The script will print which step failed.
- **Prompt source of truth**: `prompts/cascade.md` — edit that file to change tone, structure, or platform-specific rules globally.

## Examples

- `/cascade` (no args, after `/outline` approved) → finds most recent research+outline, runs automatically
- `/cascade "AI agents for non-coders"` → finds matching files for that topic
- `/cascade https://youtube.com/watch?v=abc123` → YouTube fallback mode

Here's the full map of every human decision point in the pipeline.

---

## Human-in-the-Loop Systems

There are **two kinds** — hard stops (pipeline literally waits for you) and soft reviews (pipeline runs but reminds you to check).

---

### Hard Stops — Pipeline Cannot Continue Without You

**1. Researcher — Repo selection**
Before any research runs, Claude lists all repos from the trending file and asks you to pick. The SKILL.md has a rule written in capital letters: *"Never auto-select repos without the user's explicit choice."* You also have to confirm before the actual run starts (~8 min per repo, so this gate makes sense).

**2. Ideation — Idea selection (BLOCKING GATE)**
After showing 9 ranked ideas, the skill explicitly does not suggest `/hook` yet. It asks: *"Which idea do you want to pursue? Reply with a number (1–9)."* Your choice here determines everything downstream — the hook topic, the outline structure, the titles, the distribution content. One wrong pick and the whole pipeline goes in the wrong direction.

**3. Hook — Hook selection (BLOCKING GATE)**
After showing 5 hooks, the skill says: *"do not suggest /outline until you have the answer."* It shows you all 5 Spoken Lines and asks you to pick one. The reason is mechanical — the outline `build_prompt()` injects the exact hook text you chose, so the Dopamine Ladder structure literally starts from your chosen first sentence.

**4. Cascade — Confirm before run**
Before generating the blog + Twitter + LinkedIn package, Claude says: *"Running cascade on: [topic] — research from [filename], outline from [filename]. Go?"* and waits for a yes. Unlike /hook and /ideation, this is a lighter gate — just making sure it's running against the right files.

**5. Voice Cleanup — Confirm before run**
For single-file cleanup: confirms the file path before touching anything. For batch: lists all N files and asks *"clean all?"* before running. The `--inplace` flag (overwrites the original) has an extra instruction: *"always ask first."*

---

### Soft Reviews — Pipeline Runs But Flags You to Check

**6. Outline — Review before cascade**
No hard stop, but the SKILL.md ends with: *"Review the outline for accuracy. Prep any screen shares or demos listed. Then run /cascade."* You're expected to read through the 6 Dopamine Ladder stages and verify the talking points are factually correct before turning it into distribution content.

**7. Title — Pick your own title**
`/title` runs without a confirmation gate (the SKILL.md says: *"Do not ask for confirmation — the user typed /title, they want titles."*) But the output lives in `07-Titles/` with no auto-selection. You read the 5 safe + 5 experimental options and choose manually. Nothing downstream uses a title automatically.

**8. Voice Cleanup output — No auto-publishing**
The SKILL.md ends with: *"No auto-publishing. Always review `_cleaned.md` before posting."* The cleaned file is always a separate `_cleaned.md` beside the original — you have to consciously copy it somewhere to publish.

---

### The Pattern

```
/researcher  → YOU pick repos + confirm
/ideation    → YOU pick 1 of 9 ideas (HARD STOP)
/hook        → YOU pick 1 of 5 hooks (HARD STOP)
/outline     → YOU review for accuracy (soft)
/title       → YOU choose a title (soft)
/cascade     → YOU confirm files + review output (light gate)
/short-form  → runs, you review
/voice-cleanup → YOU confirm file, then review _cleaned.md before posting
```

Every hard stop protects a **fork in the road** — a choice that, if wrong, wastes everything downstream. The soft reviews protect against **factual errors or AI-sounding content** going public.

"""Voice Cleanup — V2 De-AI'ify skill. Rewrites AI-generated content in the creator's authentic voice."""

import asyncio, argparse, logging, sys
from pathlib import Path

PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(PROJECT_ROOT))

if hasattr(sys.stdout, "reconfigure"):
    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")

from skills.utils.ai import polish

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def load_prompt_template() -> str:
    return (PROJECT_ROOT / "prompts" / "voice_cleanup.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")


async def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="De-AI'ify content — rewrite in the creator's authentic voice")
    parser.add_argument("file", nargs="?", help="Path to a markdown file to clean (omit to read from stdin)")
    parser.add_argument("--inplace", action="store_true", help="Overwrite the original file instead of writing _cleaned.md")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    if args.file:
        input_path = Path(args.file)
        if not input_path.exists():
            print(f"❌ File not found: {args.file}")
            sys.exit(1)
        text = input_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"📄 Cleaning: {input_path.name} ({len(text)} chars)...")
    else:
        if sys.stdin.isatty():
            print("Paste the text to clean (then Ctrl+Z on Windows / Ctrl+D on Unix to submit):")
        text = sys.stdin.read()
        input_path = None
        print(f"📄 Cleaning stdin input ({len(text)} chars)...")

    if not text.strip():
        print("❌ No text to clean")
        sys.exit(1)

    template = load_prompt_template()
    prompt = template.format(text=text)

    print("✍️  Running voice cleanup (Claude)...")
    result = await polish(prompt)

    if not result["success"] or not result["text"].strip():
        print(f"❌ Cleanup failed: {result.get('error', 'Empty response')}")
        sys.exit(1)

    cleaned = result["text"].strip()

    if input_path:
        if args.inplace:
            output_path = input_path
        else:
            output_path = input_path.parent / f"{input_path.stem}_cleaned{input_path.suffix}"
        output_path.write_text(cleaned, encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"""
✅ Voice cleanup complete via {result['provider']}

Output: {output_path}

--- Preview (first 300 chars) ---
{cleaned[:300]}
""")
    else:
        print(f"\n✅ Voice cleanup complete via {result['provider']}\n")
        print("--- Cleaned Output ---")
        print(cleaned)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.WARNING, format="%(levelname)s: %(message)s")
    asyncio.run(main())

The `_cleaned.md` lands **in the same folder as the original** — not in a new vault location.

The logic at [voice_cleanup.py:61](skills/voice_cleanup.py#L61):

```python
output_path = input_path.parent / f"{input_path.stem}_cleaned{input_path.suffix}"
```

So if you ran `/cascade` and it produced:
```
08-Distribution/2026-05-27_ai-agents/blog_post.md
```

Voice cleanup produces:
```
08-Distribution/2026-05-27_ai-agents/blog_post_cleaned.md   ← sits right beside it
```

The only exception is `--inplace` ([voice_cleanup.py:59](skills/voice_cleanup.py#L59)) — that overwrites the original in place, so there's only one file after. But the SKILL.md says to always ask before using that flag.

**Bottom line:** both versions live in the vault. The raw AI output and the cleaned version are side by side. You choose which one you copy out and publish.

# TODO — Separate Raw and Cleaned Output Folders

## Problem

Raw `/cascade` output and `/voice-cleanup` output currently land in the same distribution folder, mixed together:

```
08-Distribution/2026-05-27_<slug>/
  blog_post.md          ← raw AI output
  blog_post_cleaned.md  ← voice-cleaned version
  twitter_thread.md
  twitter_thread_cleaned.md
  linkedin_post.md
  linkedin_post_cleaned.md
```

This makes it unclear which file is publish-ready when browsing the vault in Obsidian.

## Desired State

```
08-Distribution/2026-05-27_<slug>/
  raw/
    blog_post.md
    twitter_thread.md
    linkedin_post.md
  cleaned/
    blog_post.md
    twitter_thread.md
    linkedin_post.md
```

`cleaned/` = publish candidate. `raw/` = AI draft kept for reference.

- [ ] [[voice_cleanup|skills/voice_cleanup.py]] — write cleaned output to `<slug>/cleaned/<original_filename>` instead of `<slug>/<stem>_cleaned.md`

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
github_trending.py — Daily AI repo pulse for Content Hub.

Run manually or via Windows Task Scheduler (see run_github_trending.bat).
Output: Content-Hub-Vault-V2/04-Trends/github_trending.md
"""

import json
import os
import subprocess
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from pathlib import Path

from dotenv import load_dotenv

# ── paths ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
load_dotenv(ROOT / ".env")
OUTPUT = ROOT / "Content-Hub-Vault-V2" / "04-Trends" / "github_trending.md"
LOG_DIR = ROOT / "logs"

# ── config ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
GITHUB_TOKEN = os.getenv("GITHUB_TOKEN", "")
# 3 searches (one per topic) against the 30-day window covers both windows.
# GitHub Search API doesn't support OR across topic qualifiers with date filters.
# Unauthenticated limit: 10 req/min. 3 calls is safe; add GITHUB_TOKEN for 5000/hr.
AI_TOPICS = ["llm", "ai", "machine-learning"]


# ── GitHub API ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _gh_headers() -> dict:
    h = {
        "Accept": "application/vnd.github+json",
        "X-GitHub-Api-Version": "2022-11-28",
        "User-Agent": "content-hub-trending/1.0",
    }
    if GITHUB_TOKEN:
        h["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {GITHUB_TOKEN}"
    return h


def _search_one_topic(topic: str, since_date: str, per_page: int = 10) -> list[dict]:
    q = f"topic:{topic} created:>{since_date}"
    url = (
        "https://api.github.com/search/repositories?"
        + urllib.parse.urlencode({"q": q, "sort": "stars", "order": "desc", "per_page": per_page})
    )
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers=_gh_headers())
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=15) as resp:
        return json.loads(resp.read()).get("items", [])


def search_repos(since_date: str, fetch: int = 30) -> list[dict]:
    """Return raw GitHub repo items created after since_date, merged across AI topics, sorted by stars."""
    seen: set[int] = set()
    merged: list[dict] = []
    for topic in AI_TOPICS:
        for item in _search_one_topic(topic, since_date, per_page=15):
            if item["id"] not in seen:
                seen.add(item["id"])
                merged.append(item)
    merged.sort(key=lambda r: r["stargazers_count"], reverse=True)
    return merged[:fetch]


def enrich(raw: dict, now: datetime) -> dict:
    created = datetime.fromisoformat(raw["created_at"].replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    age = max(1, (now - created).days)
    return {
        "name": raw["full_name"],
        "description": (raw.get("description") or "").strip(),
        "language": raw.get("language") or "—",
        "stars": raw["stargazers_count"],
        "velocity": round(raw["stargazers_count"] / age, 1),
        "url": raw["html_url"],
    }


# ── Claude pick ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def claude_picks(repos_7d: list[dict], repos_30d: list[dict]) -> tuple[str, str, str, str]:
    """Return (name_7d, reason_7d, name_30d, reason_30d). Uses claude CLI (Pro plan auth)."""

    def fmt(repos: list[dict]) -> str:
        return "\n".join(
            f"{i+1}. {r['name']} | {r['stars']:,} stars | {r['velocity']}/day | {r['language']}\n"
            f"   {r['description']}\n   {r['url']}"
            for i, r in enumerate(repos)
        )

    prompt = (
        "You are a tech content strategist for an AI-focused YouTube channel.\n\n"
        "Pick ONE repo from each list as the best candidate for a YouTube tutorial or explainer.\n"
        "Criteria: genuine novelty, teaching potential, audience interest, not already overexposed.\n\n"
        f"LAST 7 DAYS — TOP {len(repos_7d)}:\n{fmt(repos_7d)}\n\n"
        f"LAST 30 DAYS — TOP {len(repos_30d)}:\n{fmt(repos_30d)}\n\n"
        "Respond with ONLY valid JSON, no markdown fences:\n"
        '{"pick_7d": {"name": "owner/repo", "reason": "1-2 sentences"}, '
        '"pick_30d": {"name": "owner/repo", "reason": "1-2 sentences"}}'
    )

    result = subprocess.run(
        "claude",
        input=prompt,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        encoding="utf-8",
        timeout=60,
        shell=True,
    )
    if result.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"claude CLI failed: {result.stderr.strip()}")

    raw = result.stdout.strip()
    # Strip markdown fences if claude wraps the JSON anyway
    if raw.startswith("```"):
        raw = raw.split("```")[1]
        if raw.startswith("json"):
            raw = raw[4:]
    parsed = json.loads(raw.strip())
    p7 = parsed["pick_7d"]
    p30 = parsed["pick_30d"]
    return p7["name"], p7["reason"], p30["name"], p30["reason"]


# ── Claude deep dive ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def claude_deep_dive(repo: dict) -> dict:
    """Return detailed breakdown for one repo: problem, how_it_works, use_cases, getting_started."""
    prompt = (
        f"Repo: {repo['name']}\n"
        f"Description: {repo['description']}\n"
        f"Language: {repo['language']}\n"
        f"Stars: {repo['stars']:,}\n"
        f"URL: {repo['url']}\n\n"
        "Using ONLY the information above (do not fetch URLs or external data), write a breakdown "
        "for a tech content creator. Respond with ONLY valid JSON, no markdown fences:\n"
        '{"problem": "What real problem does this solve? (2-3 sentences)", '
        '"how_it_works": "How does it work technically? (2-3 sentences)", '
        '"use_cases": ["use case 1", "use case 2", "use case 3"], '
        '"getting_started": "How would a developer get started with this? (1-2 sentences)"}'
    )
    result = subprocess.run(
        "claude",
        input=prompt,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        encoding="utf-8",
        timeout=60,
        shell=True,
    )
    if result.returncode != 0:
        return {}
    raw = result.stdout.strip()
    if raw.startswith("```"):
        raw = raw.split("```")[1]
        if raw.startswith("json"):
            raw = raw[4:]
    try:
        return json.loads(raw.strip())
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        return {}


def write_repo_file(repo: dict, dive: dict, trends_dir: Path) -> None:
    if not dive:
        return
    slug = repo["name"].replace("/", "_")
    folder = trends_dir / slug
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    use_cases = "\n".join(f"- {uc}" for uc in dive.get("use_cases", []))
    today = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    content = "\n".join([
        f"# {repo['name']}",
        "",
        f"> {repo['description']}",
        "",
        f"**Language:** {repo['language']} · **Stars:** {repo['stars']:,} · **Velocity:** {repo['velocity']}/day · [GitHub]({repo['url']})",
        "",
        f"*Captured {today}*",
        "",
        "---",
        "",
        "## What problem does it solve?",
        "",
        dive.get("problem", ""),
        "",
        "## How it works",
        "",
        dive.get("how_it_works", ""),
        "",
        "## Best use cases",
        "",
        use_cases,
        "",
        "## Getting started",
        "",
        dive.get("getting_started", ""),
    ])
    (folder / f"{slug}.md").write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")


# ── render ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _table(repos: list[dict], highlight: str) -> list[str]:
    rows = [
        "| Repo | Stars | ⚡ Stars/day | Language | Description |",
        "|------|------:|------------:|----------|-------------|",
    ]
    for r in repos:
        flag = " 🎯" if r["name"] == highlight else ""
        desc = r["description"]
        if len(desc) > 75:
            desc = desc[:72] + "…"
        rows.append(
            f"| [{r['name']}]({r['url']}){flag}"
            f" | {r['stars']:,} | {r['velocity']} | {r['language']} | {desc} |"
        )
    return rows


def render(repos_7d, repos_30d, name_7d, reason_7d, name_30d, reason_30d) -> str:
    today = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    url_7d = next((r["url"] for r in repos_7d if r["name"] == name_7d), "")
    url_30d = next((r["url"] for r in repos_30d if r["name"] == name_30d), "")
    slug_7d = name_7d.replace("/", "_")
    slug_30d = name_30d.replace("/", "_")

    lines = [
        f"# GitHub Trending AI Repos — {today}",
        "",
        "> Auto-generated daily. 🎯 = Claude's pick for best video topic.",
        "",
        "---",
        "",
        "## Last 7 Days — Top 10",
        "",
        *_table(repos_7d, name_7d),
        "",
        "## Last 30 Days — Top 5",
        "",
        *_table(repos_30d, name_30d),
        "",
        "---",
        "",
        "## Claude's Daily Picks",
        "",
        f"### 7-day pick → [{name_7d}]({url_7d})",
        "",
        reason_7d,
        "",
        f"→ Deep dive: [[{slug_7d}/{slug_7d}]]",
        "",
        f"### 30-day pick → [{name_30d}]({url_30d})",
        "",
        reason_30d,
        "",
        f"→ Deep dive: [[{slug_30d}/{slug_30d}]]",
        "",
        "---",
        f"*Generated {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')}"
        " · [GitHub Trending](https://github.com/trending)*",
    ]
    return "\n".join(lines)


# ── main ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def main() -> None:
    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    cutoff_7d = now - timedelta(days=7)
    date_30d = (now - timedelta(days=30)).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")

    # One search against 30-day window; split client-side into both windows.
    print("Fetching trending repos (30-day window)...")
    raw = search_repos(date_30d, fetch=40)
    all_repos = [enrich(r, now) for r in raw]

    created_map = {r["full_name"]: r["created_at"] for r in raw}
    repos_7d = [
        r for r in all_repos
        if datetime.fromisoformat(created_map[r["name"]].replace("Z", "+00:00")) >= cutoff_7d
    ][:10]

    seen_7d = {r["name"] for r in repos_7d}
    repos_30d = [r for r in all_repos if r["name"] not in seen_7d][:5]

    print(f"  7-day: {len(repos_7d)} repos | 30-day extra: {len(repos_30d)} repos")
    print("Asking Claude for picks...")
    name_7d, reason_7d, name_30d, reason_30d = claude_picks(repos_7d, repos_30d)

    OUTPUT.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    LOG_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    OUTPUT.write_text(
        render(repos_7d, repos_30d, name_7d, reason_7d, name_30d, reason_30d),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )

    # Every shortlisted repo gets its own subfolder — not just the picks.
    all_shortlisted = repos_7d + repos_30d
    print(f"Generating deep dives for all {len(all_shortlisted)} shortlisted repos...")
    for i, repo in enumerate(all_shortlisted, 1):
        print(f"  [{i}/{len(all_shortlisted)}] {repo['name']}")
        dive = claude_deep_dive(repo)
        write_repo_file(repo, dive, OUTPUT.parent)
    print(f"Done. Written to {OUTPUT.parent}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Research Guardrails — Agent Orchestration Plan

Plan file: `C:\Users\madhu\.claude\plans\here-s-the-full-audit-parsed-goblet.md`

## What We're Building
Baking 5 guardrails into `skills/yt_pipeline.py` and `skills/researcher.py` so every research run scores 9/10 by default.

The 5 guardrails:
1. Primary-source pre-flight (arxiv, github, docs harvested before chat starts)
2. Question-budget tracker with dedup (`QuestionPlan` class)
3. Adaptive follow-up drilling (Gemini 2.5 Flash → Claude fallback)
4. Competitive landscape question (always asked)
5. Content-angle battery (3 fixed questions at end of every run)

## Files Touched
| File | Status |
|---|---|
| NEW `skills/research_sources.py` | Agent A |
| NEW `skills/research_plan.py` | Agent A |
| NEW `prompts/research_followups.md` | Agent B |
| MODIFY `prompts/researcher.md` | Agent B |
| MODIFY `prompts/yt_pipeline.md` | Agent B |
| MODIFY `skills/yt_pipeline.py` | Agent C |
| MODIFY `skills/researcher.py` | Agent D |
| MODIFY `skills/ideation.py` | Agent E |

## Agent Architecture
- 5 agents, 3 phases
- **Phase 1 (parallel):** Agent A (Foundation) + Agent B (Prompts)
- **Phase 2 (parallel, blocked on Phase 1):** Agent C (yt_pipeline.py) + Agent D (researcher.py)
- **Phase 3 (blocked on Phase 2):** Agent E (ideation.py + verification)

## Execution Model
- Pure filesystem handoff — agents read/write disk only, no relay through orchestrator
- Sentinel files in `.agents/` mark completion (existence-only check, no content read)
- State file: `.agents/orchestration_state.json` tracks phase/agent status for resume
- Context passing: Phase 2+ agent prompts are pre-written and self-contained (read from disk directly)

**Why:** Keeps orchestrator context window clean — only boolean checks between phases, never code content.

## Resume Mechanism
State file `.agents/orchestration_state.json` is source of truth. On resume, check which agents have `.done` sentinels and skip them. Launch only incomplete agents.

2	
3	import logging
4	from notebooklm.types import ReportSuggestion
5	from skills.utils.ai import generate
6	
7	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
8	
9	
10	async def pick_best_report(
11	    suggestions: list[ReportSuggestion],
12	    goal: str,
13	) -> ReportSuggestion | None:
14	    """Pick the best report suggestion from a list using NIM.
15	
16	    Args:
17	        suggestions: List of ReportSuggestion objects from get_suggested_reports.
18	        goal: Either "explainer" or "technical" — the target report type.
19	
20	    Returns:
21	        Best matching ReportSuggestion, or None if no good match found.
22	    """
23	    if not suggestions:
24	        return None
25	
26	    # Build a prompt listing the suggestions
27	    suggestion_text = "\n".join(
28	        f"- {s.title}: {s.description}"
29	        for s in suggestions
30	    )
31	
32	    prompt = f"""Given these report suggestions:
33	
34	{suggestion_text}
35	
36	Which one best matches the goal of creating a {goal} report?
37	Return ONLY the exact title of the best match (no explanation).
38	If none match well, return "NONE"."""
39	
40	    result = await generate(prompt, cascade=["nim"])
41	    if not result.get("success"):
42	        logger.warning("NIM report picker failed: %s", result.get("error"))
43	        return None
44	
45	    best_title = result.get("text", "").strip()
46	    if best_title == "NONE" or not best_title:
47	        return None
48	
49	    # Find and return the matching suggestion
50	    for suggestion in suggestions:

"""NIM-powered report suggestion picker."""

import logging
from notebooklm.types import ReportSuggestion
from skills.utils.ai import generate

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


async def pick_best_report(
    suggestions: list[ReportSuggestion],
    goal: str,
) -> ReportSuggestion | None:
    """Pick the best report suggestion from a list using NIM.

    Args:
        suggestions: List of ReportSuggestion objects from get_suggested_reports.
        goal: Either "explainer" or "technical" — the target report type.

    Returns:
        Best matching ReportSuggestion, or None if no good match found.
    """
    if not suggestions:
        return None

    # Build a prompt listing the suggestions
    suggestion_text = "\n".join(
        f"- {s.title}: {s.description}"
        for s in suggestions
    )

    prompt = f"""Given these report suggestions:

{suggestion_text}

Which one best matches the goal of creating a {goal} report?
Return ONLY the exact title of the best match (no explanation).
If none match well, return "NONE"."""

    result = await generate(prompt, cascade=["nim"])
    if not result.get("success"):
        logger.warning("NIM report picker failed: %s", result.get("error"))
        return None

    best_title = result.get("text", "").strip()
    if best_title == "NONE" or not best_title:
        return None

    # Find and return the matching suggestion
    for suggestion in suggestions:
        if suggestion.title.strip() == best_title:
            return suggestion

    logger.warning("NIM returned title '%s' but no exact match found", best_title)
    return None

"""Primary-source pre-flight for the research pipeline.

Harvests primary sources (arxiv papers, GitHub repos, official docs, PDFs)
from YT video descriptions via yt-dlp, then falls back to a Gemini prompt
backstop if fewer than 5 credible hits are found from scraping.
"""

import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys

# Trusted primary source patterns
_ARXIV = re.compile(r'https?://arxiv\.org/(?:abs|pdf)/[\w./-]+')
_GITHUB = re.compile(r'https?://github\.com/([^/\s#?\'"]+/[^/\s#?\'"]+)')
_PDF = re.compile(r'https?://\S+\.pdf(?:\?\S*)?')
_OFFICIAL = re.compile(
    r'https?://(?:docs\.[^\s]+|[^\s]+\.readthedocs\.io[^\s]*'
    r'|huggingface\.co/[^\s]+|pytorch\.org[^\s]*|tensorflow\.org[^\s]*'
    r'|openai\.com/research[^\s]*)'
)

# Low-trust domains to reject
_REJECT = re.compile(
    r'(?:reddit\.com|twitter\.com|x\.com|youtube\.com|youtu\.be'
    r'|medium\.com|substack\.com|tiktok\.com|instagram\.com)',
    re.I,
)


def _extract_from_text(text: str) -> list[str]:
    found: list[str] = []
    for m in _ARXIV.finditer(text):
        found.append(m.group(0))
    for m in _GITHUB.finditer(text):
        found.append(f"https://github.com/{m.group(1)}")
    for m in _PDF.finditer(text):
        found.append(m.group(0))
    for m in _OFFICIAL.finditer(text):
        found.append(m.group(0))
    return [u for u in found if not _REJECT.search(u)]


def _scrape_yt_descriptions(seed_urls: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Run yt-dlp --get-description on each URL, regex-extract primary links."""
    collected: list[str] = []
    for url in seed_urls:
        try:
            result = subprocess.run(
                [sys.executable, "-m", "yt_dlp",
                 "--get-description", "--no-playlist", "--quiet", url],
                capture_output=True,
                text=True,
                encoding="utf-8",
                timeout=30,
            )
            if result.stdout:
                collected.extend(_extract_from_text(result.stdout))
        except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, Exception):
            continue
    return collected


async def _gemini_backstop(topic: str) -> list[str]:
    """Ask Gemini to suggest primary source URLs from its training data."""
    try:
        from skills.utils.ai import generate
    except ImportError:
        return []

    prompt = (
        f"List the most relevant primary sources for: {topic}\n\n"
        "Return ONLY a JSON array of real, existing URLs from trusted sources:\n"
        "- arxiv.org papers (e.g. https://arxiv.org/abs/XXXX.XXXXX)\n"
        "- github.com repositories (e.g. https://github.com/owner/repo)\n"
        "- official project documentation\n"
        "- peer-reviewed venues\n\n"
        'Format: ["https://...", ...]\n'
        "Return 5-8 URLs. Return [] if you cannot identify credible primaries."
    )

    result = await generate(prompt, cascade=["claude", "nim"])
    if not result["success"] or not result["text"]:
        return []

    text = result["text"].strip()
    match = re.search(r'\[.*?\]', text, re.DOTALL)
    if not match:
        return []
    try:
        urls = json.loads(match.group(0))
        return [u for u in urls if isinstance(u, str) and u.startswith("http")]
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
        return []


def _dedupe_cap(urls: list[str], cap: int = 8) -> list[str]:
    seen: set[str] = set()
    result: list[str] = []
    for u in urls:
        u = u.rstrip(".,;)")
        if u not in seen:
            seen.add(u)
            result.append(u)
        if len(result) >= cap:
            break
    return result


async def collect_primary_sources(
    topic: str, seed_urls: list[str]
) -> tuple[list[str], dict]:
    """Return (primary_urls, metadata).

    Step 1 — scrape: yt-dlp description regex-extract for each seed URL.
    Step 2 — backstop: if scrape found < 5, ask Gemini for likely primaries.
    """
    raw = _scrape_yt_descriptions(seed_urls)
    strategy = "scrape"

    if len(raw) < 5:
        backstop = await _gemini_backstop(topic)
        if backstop:
            raw = raw + backstop
            strategy = "scrape+search-backstop"

    urls = _dedupe_cap(raw)
    return urls, {"primary_sources_found": len(urls), "strategy": strategy}

Now I have a complete picture. Here's how the eval and guardrail systems work:

---

## Eval Systems

These are **structured test suites** that define what correct behavior looks like for each skill — like unit tests, but for Claude's conversational behavior.

### Where they live
Each skill has its own workspace: `.claude/skills/<skill>-workspace/`
```
evals/evals.json          ← the test cases
iteration-1/
  eval-<name>/eval_metadata.json   ← individual test input + assertions
  eval_review.html                  ← visual results dashboard
```

### What they test
Each eval is a **prompt → assertions** pair. Example from `/cascade`:

- **Input:** "I just approved my ai-agents outline, let's cascade now"
- **Assertions checked:**
  - Did Claude find both the research brief AND outline by filename?
  - Did it ask for confirmation exactly once (not multiple prompts)?
  - Did the filenames appear in the confirmation message?
  - Did it use `--research-file` and `--outline-file` flags (not a URL)?
  - Did it preview the Twitter hook after completion?
  - Did it mention replacing `[VIDEO_LINK]`?
  - Did it suggest `/short-form` as the next step?

The evals are **not automated tests** — they're specifications that a human reviews using `eval_review.html`. The HTML file is a browser-based dashboard for scoring runs.

**Coverage:** cascade, researcher, hook, outline, voice-cleanup, title, short-form, orchestrate — every major skill has its own eval suite.

---

## Guardrail Systems

These are **runtime quality controls** baked into the research pipeline to prevent bad output from reaching the vault.

### 1. Source Filter (`research_sources.py`)
A regex-based allowlist/blocklist that runs on every URL before it enters the research pipeline:

- **Allowed:** arxiv papers, GitHub repos, official docs (readthedocs, HuggingFace, PyTorch, OpenAI research), PDFs
- **Blocked:** Reddit, Twitter/X, YouTube, Medium, Substack, TikTok, Instagram

If `< 5` credible sources are found from scraping YouTube descriptions, it fires a **backstop** — asks Claude/NIM to suggest primary sources from training data. This ensures every research run starts from trusted material.

### 2. Question Budget Tracker (`research_plan.py` — `QuestionPlan`)
Controls how many questions get asked to NotebookLM during a research session:

- Default budget: **12 questions**
- **Dedup filter:** normalizes questions (strips filler words, lowercases) and blocks any new question with >60% word overlap with an already-asked question
- **Adaptive follow-ups:** after each answer, asks the AI to generate 0-2 drilling follow-ups, queued within the remaining budget
- Emits stats at the end: questions asked, deduped count, follow-ups generated, budget remaining

### 3. NIM Judge (`helpers/nim_picker.py`)
An LLM-as-judge step that runs *before* research begins:

- Gets a list of `ReportSuggestion` objects from NotebookLM
- Asks NIM: "which suggestion best matches the goal: `explainer` or `technical`?"
- Returns the best match — or `None` if nothing fits, which halts that code path

This is a **quality gate** — prevents a mismatched report structure from propagating through the pipeline.

### 4. SKILL.md BLOCKING GATEs (human-in-the-loop)
Hard stops written into skill definition files that prevent the pipeline from auto-advancing:

- `/ideation` → "Which idea do you want to pursue? Reply with a number (1–9)." — will not suggest `/hook` until answered
- `/hook` → shows 5 hooks, "do not suggest /outline until you have the answer"
- `/researcher` → "Never auto-select repos without the user's explicit choice"

These are behavioral guardrails enforced through Claude's instruction-following, not code.

---

**Summary in plain terms:**

| System | Type | Purpose |
|--------|------|---------|
| `evals.json` + `eval_review.html` | Specification + human review | Verify skill behavior is correct before shipping changes |
| `research_sources.py` | Runtime filter | Block low-trust sources from entering research |
| `research_plan.py` `QuestionPlan` | Runtime budget | Prevent redundant/runaway NotebookLM questions |
| `nim_picker.py` | LLM judge | Pick best report structure before research runs |
| SKILL.md BLOCKING GATE | Behavioral instruction | Human approval required at key pipeline decision points |

content.text:
## Canva API Research Summary

**1. Public API Status**: Canva's **Connect API is publicly available** (not invite-only). OAuth 2.0 with PKCE secures access. Some endpoints are production-ready; others (like Design Editing API) remain in beta.

**2. Programmatic Design Creation**: Limited. Canva's Connect API can create designs and manage existing ones, but **full design creation and editing from scratch requires Enterprise access**. Standard API users get design workflow integration, not full generative capabilities.

**3. What It Can Do**:
- Create designs from templates
- Read/update layout and element positioning
- Manage assets and resources
- Integrate Canva editor into third-party apps (Apps SDK)
- User and team management (Admin/SCIM APIs)

**Cannot do** (programmatically): AI-powered design generation, advanced content creation without the UI.

**4. Authentication**: OAuth 2.0 (Authorization Code + PKCE). POST to `https://api.canva.com/rest/v1/oauth/token` for access tokens.

**5. Python/REST Support**: 
- **No official Python SDK**. Canva publishes OpenAPI spec at `https://www.canva.dev/sources/connect/api/latest/api.yml` — use openapi-generator to build your own client.
- REST endpoints fully documented at canva.dev/docs/connect.

**Bottom line**: Good for design workflow automation and template-based work; poor fit if you need programmatic generative design creation. Enterprise tier unlocks more.

Sources:
- [Canva Connect API Documentation](https://www.canva.dev/docs/connect/)
- [Authentication - Canva Connect APIs](https://www.canva.dev/docs/connect/authentication/)
- [API requests and responses - Canva Connect](https://www.canva.dev/docs/connect/api-requests-responses/)
- [Canva Developers](https://www.canva.com/developers/)

This skill guides creation of distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces that avoid generic "AI slop" aesthetics. Implement real working code with exceptional attention to aesthetic details and creative choices.

The user provides frontend requirements: a component, page, application, or interface to build. They may include context about the purpose, audience, or technical constraints.

## Design Thinking

Before coding, understand the context and commit to a BOLD aesthetic direction:
- **Purpose**: What problem does this interface solve? Who uses it?
- **Tone**: Pick an extreme: brutally minimal, maximalist chaos, retro-futuristic, organic/natural, luxury/refined, playful/toy-like, editorial/magazine, brutalist/raw, art deco/geometric, soft/pastel, industrial/utilitarian, etc. There are so many flavors to choose from. Use these for inspiration but design one that is true to the aesthetic direction.
- **Constraints**: Technical requirements (framework, performance, accessibility).
- **Differentiation**: What makes this UNFORGETTABLE? What's the one thing someone will remember?

**CRITICAL**: Choose a clear conceptual direction and execute it with precision. Bold maximalism and refined minimalism both work - the key is intentionality, not intensity.

Then implement working code (HTML/CSS/JS, React, Vue, etc.) that is:
- Production-grade and functional
- Visually striking and memorable
- Cohesive with a clear aesthetic point-of-view
- Meticulously refined in every detail

## Frontend Aesthetics Guidelines

Focus on:
- **Typography**: Choose fonts that are beautiful, unique, and interesting. Avoid generic fonts like Arial and Inter; opt instead for distinctive choices that elevate the frontend's aesthetics; unexpected, characterful font choices. Pair a distinctive display font with a refined body font.
- **Color & Theme**: Commit to a cohesive aesthetic. Use CSS variables for consistency. Dominant colors with sharp accents outperform timid, evenly-distributed palettes.
- **Motion**: Use animations for effects and micro-interactions. Prioritize CSS-only solutions for HTML. Use Motion library for React when available. Focus on high-impact moments: one well-orchestrated page load with staggered reveals (animation-delay) creates more delight than scattered micro-interactions. Use scroll-triggering and hover states that surprise.
- **Spatial Composition**: Unexpected layouts. Asymmetry. Overlap. Diagonal flow. Grid-breaking elements. Generous negative space OR controlled density.
- **Backgrounds & Visual Details**: Create atmosphere and depth rather than defaulting to solid colors. Add contextual effects and textures that match the overall aesthetic. Apply creative forms like gradient meshes, noise textures, geometric patterns, layered transparencies, dramatic shadows, decorative borders, custom cursors, and grain overlays.

NEVER use generic AI-generated aesthetics like overused font families (Inter, Roboto, Arial, system fonts), cliched color schemes (particularly purple gradients on white backgrounds), predictable layouts and component patterns, and cookie-cutter design that lacks context-specific character.

Interpret creatively and make unexpected choices that feel genuinely designed for the context. No design should be the same. Vary between light and dark themes, different fonts, different aesthetics. NEVER converge on common choices (Space Grotesk, for example) across generations.

**IMPORTANT**: Match implementation complexity to the aesthetic vision. Maximalist designs need elaborate code with extensive animations and effects. Minimalist or refined designs need restraint, precision, and careful attention to spacing, typography, and subtle details. Elegance comes from executing the vision well.

Remember: Claude is capable of extraordinary creative work. Don't hold back, show what can truly be created when thinking outside the box and committing fully to a distinctive vision.
